subject: Analyses from same population returning distinctly different results

messages.author: 4c4091a92f5b965e
messages.subject: Analyses from same population returning distinctly different results
parts:
Hello Dr. Broman and Google Doc members!
I have three problems that I am currently struggling with and would appreciate any help you can offer. I am working in a plant model with five chromosomes. I am studying many phenotypes, but am measuring the phenotype four ways: Ambient, Elevated, Diff, Ratio. For the purposes here, I am only looking at cell density (SD).

The second problem:

My RIL population has 167 core lines from a much larger 430 set. Initially, there were only 69 markers. Since I started the project, another group has taken a subset of 211 lines from the full 430 set and identified about 578 markers. The trouble is- only 63 of the offspring lines from the 211 subset are also included in the original 167 subset.

To be more clear- I have phenotypes for 167 lines with 69 markers. Within the 167 lines, I have a subset of 63 lines that have 578 markers. So I can run the analyses with a large number of recombination events (more lines) and low marker resolution; or I can run the analyses with a low number of recombination events (less lines) and high marker resolution.

I opted to run both. So here is the problem: the graphs between the two populations look very different.

Core 167 lines:
(Graph not shown)

Updated 63 lines:
(Graph not shown)

These two plots are for the same phenotype (SD) but for the two different popualtions subsets. Keep in mind that the 63 lines are all present in the original 167. In the first plot I have three markers, one in my Ratio measurement (black line) and two in my Elevated measurement (green), but neither of these appear in the second plot. In the second plot, I have quite a few peaks in my Ambient (red line) compared to none in the first plot.

So my question is- how common is this? I know it is common for different populations within the same species, but I don’t know how to explain this for a subset population within

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Analyses from same population returning distinctly different results
parts:
There are all kinds of explanations for such differences. You might also look at the subset of 63 lines with the reduced number of markers.

karl
